essing the numeric relationship between `ju/jv/ku/kv` (unsafe — a wrong guess about e.g. a fixed offset would silently corrupt other inputs), I recover the true producer→consumer edges generically at runtime:

- Track, as the original index order is scanned once, the (unique) prior iteration that last wrote each `u`/`v` location.
- For each iteration `i`, its only real predecessor is `max(last_writer_v[kv[i]], last_writer_u[ku[i]])` (or none). Assign `level[i] = level[predecessor] + 1`, else `0`.
- Iterations sharing a level touch no location that any other iteration on that level writes or reads (by construction), so they are mutually independent and can execute in any order/in parallel. Levels themselves must still run in ascending order since values from level `L` feed level `L+1`.
- Bucket iterations by level (prefix-sum bucketing, O(n)), then run an outer sequential loop over levels and an inner loop over each level's members that performs the exact original two statements, in their original order, on values already finalized by lower levels — so the sequence of floating-point operations is identical to the original sweep; only the visitation order of independent iterations changes.

This is a general, correctness-preserving restructuring that doesn't assume any specific structure of `ju/jv/ku/kv` beyond what DiscoPoP actually observed (injective writers, backward-only RAW). All auxiliary buffers (`last_writer_u/v`, `level`, `level_count`, `level_start`, `fill_pos`, `order`) are heap-allocated via `malloc`/`free` since their size scales with `LEN_1D`. The inner per-level loop (`for (long p = lo; p < hi; p++)`) is the outermost loop that can be made independent and is the Do-All candidate; the level loop that wraps it is left sequential because it carries the genuine dependency. Added `#include <stdlib.h>` for `malloc`/`free`; the two protected lines (`#include "evk/k17.h"` and `PB_MAIN(kernel_k17)`) are untouched, and the function's name/signature is unchanged.
